stories.title: Death toll from Nepal-Tibet flash floods rises to 750
stories.summary: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet from last week's catastrophic floods has hit 750 with 3,044 missing, authorities said, while rescuers moved to higher ground as rain swelled river levels. Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-Tibet border by a mudslide from Wednesday's glacier collapse could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into rivers in Nepal. The Red Cross estimates that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart in a telephone call yesterday that the mudslide was their "most severe cross-border disaster" in recent years and that rescue operations were of unprecedented difficulty and complexity, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported.

stories.title: Dáil fuel vote 'significant intervention' - Harris
stories.summary: Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris has described today's Dáil vote to defer the increases in motor fuel excise duty as a "significant intervention". Mr Harris added that the Government is "carefully" monitoring the global energy crisis and that any other suggestion is "dishonest politics". TDs backed Government plans to defer the increases, which had been planned for September and October, by 104 votes to 49. The cuts to excise duty on petrol and diesel are now set to be phased out over a period from November to the end of February.

stories.title: Forum recommends tackling energy costs for businesses
stories.summary: Energy has been identified as the principal contributor to rising business costs by an advisory forum established by the Government. The Cost of Business Advisory Forum has issued its final report setting out 63 recommendations to boost competitiveness and cut costs. The report found that the Government should consider the feasibility of a new scheme to reduce prices for large energy intensive business users. It also highlighted the importance of price transparency and easier switching for non-domestic customers.

stories.title: Fed has 'work to do' if above-target inflation remains
stories.summary: The US Federal Reserve will "have work to do" if policymakers are not confident that underlying inflation is returning to its 2% target, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said today. His remarks acknowledged that financial conditions do not appear restrictive and marked the closest he has come to acknowledging interest rate hikes may be needed to ease price pressures. "Here is my standard - we must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do. That's our job ... our mandate ... and our charge to keep," Warsh said in a remarks prepared for delivery to the Fed's Jackson Hole economic symposium in Wyoming. While much of the 16-page address focused on large issues, like the influence of artificial intelligence, that Warsh feels will be critical in the long run, it also included some key acknowledgements - including that "short-term interest rates are the predominant tool to achieve the dual mandate."

stories.title: Hope and horror: Families in Nepal await news of missing
stories.summary: The walls of Kathmandu's largest hospital have been transformed in recent days. Colourful posters have begun popping up everywhere, their subjects’ smiling, happy faces at odds with the messages carefully printed on the paper in English and Nepali. The photographs serve to humanise a tragedy that has made headlines around the world this week, with videos of the destruction and devastation being viewed millions of times. The posters bring to focus the lives and livelihoods of the people impacted - a baby in blue dungarees in his mother’s arms, a newly-married couple, a grandfather on pilgrimage.

stories.title: Cremen eyes another medal as mixed double sculls progress
stories.summary: Mags Cremen remains in the hunt for another medal at the World Rowing Championships as the mixed double sculls crew progressed from Sunday's semi-final. On Friday Cremen claimed gold in the women's double sculls alongside Zoe Hyde, and was back in the water this morning alongside Konan Pazzaia as Ireland looks to defend the crown they won last year in the event's maiden year on the schedule. In 2025 Fintan McCarthy secured gold alongside Cremen, while now it is Pazzaia in the boat, with Cremen occupying the stroke seat. The three fastest qualifiers – Ireland, Switzerland and the USA – set the early pace and by the halfway stage less than half a second separated the three crews, with the Swiss leading Ireland through.

stories.title: Tribe veteran on rewarding journey to ultimate glory
stories.summary: A few weeks have now passed since their nail-biting win over Kerry at Croke Park, but Galway's All-Ireland success still feels like a deeply satisfying one for experienced defender Sarah Ní Loingsigh. A senior panellist since 2011, the Naomh Anna Leitir Mór stalwart lined out at full-back when the Tribeswomen collected the Brendan Martin Cup for just the second time in their history with a tense 2-07 to 0-12 showpiece victory at the expense of the Kingdom. The Connacht side had been pushing hard in the latter stages of the championship in recent seasons and their 2026 campaign saw them taking the final step on their journey back to the top of ladies football. This led to scenes of immense joy in the minutes that followed their one-point triumph at the Jones’ Road venue and this mood was maintained upon the squad’s return home to the west a day later.

stories.title: Duran gives Celtic welcome tonic after tough week
stories.summary: Camilo Duran's performance provided some sort of tonic for Celtic fans following their European disappointment as the Colombian netted a double in a 2-1 win over Falkirk. Duran was handed his preferred position of centre-forward in place of the injured Kasper Hogh and he delivered two striker’s goals in the opening 29 minutes while setting up several team-mates for chances. Celtic missed a series of first-half opportunities but Falkirk improved after the break and pressed their hosts much higher up the park. Their ambition was rewarded by Colby Donovan’s own goal in the 72nd minute but Celtic pushed them back for the rest of the game without finding the net again.

stories.title: Round up: Pre-season defeats in France for Irish sides
stories.summary: Leinster, Munster and Connacht all began their pre-season campaigns with defeats in France, although their first outings of the summer were against sides who are all bracing for their first Pro14 outings next week. A youthful Leinster side came up just short in Lyon as they came out the wrong side of an entertaining 31-29 contest, while Munster improved after a dreadful first half to eventually lose 47-26 in La Rochelle. Connacht, meanwhile, let a 16-point lead slip in the final quarter against Vannes in Brittany, as Mack Hansen looked sharp on his return in a 36-35 defeat. Leinster's night in Lyon started brightly as Gus McCarthy (above), who was captain for the night, mauled his way over the line on three minutes, with Caspar Gabriel converting to give them a 7-0 lead.

stories.title: Slí na Samhlaíochta - celebrating the legacy of Manchán Magan
stories.summary: Musical Director Simon O'Reilly introduces Slí na Samhlaíochta/The Way of Imagination, a live performance coming to the National Concert Hall this October that brings together spoken word, music, and visual art in an exploration of the concept of Tír na nÓg through the work of the late author, traveller, broadcaster and documentary maker Manchán Magan. Slí na Samhlaíochta began at the Hedge School Festival in Doolin in 2023, an event I co-founded to bring musicians, writers and visual artists together to create new work. For the closing performance, Manchán Magan brought a spoken-word piece inspired by Tír na nÓg and An Saol Eile, the Otherworld of Irish tradition. Myles O'Reilly and I created a live score around his words, while Crosby Dunkley developed the visuals that accompanied the performance. None of us expected the response. From the opening moments there was a stillness in the room that is difficult to describe. The audience seemed completely immersed and, afterwards, many spoke about how deeply they had been affected. I came away feeling we had created something that deserved another life.

stories.title: How can you spot a liar? An expert weighs in
stories.summary: With a new season of The Traitors Ireland this Sunday, 30 August, Dr Sabina Brennan, Psychologist & Neuroscientist, joined Drivetime to discuss why we lie and whether you can spot a liar. We've all heard you can spot a liar by their tells: scratching their nose, breaking eye contact, tripping over their words or changing their voice. In theory, we should be able to notice when they're being deceitful because they will start acting abnormally. But Brennan explains that these tells are mostly "myths". In reality, lying is a "natural ability", she says. "I think the important thing to remember about The Traitors is that it's a game, so it's not about people necessarily becoming dishonest. They've accepted a temporary role in which deception is permitted, and it's expected, and it's even rewarded.

stories.title: GP in prescriptions probe will comply with suspension
stories.summary: A Co Wicklow-based doctor has promised under oath to comply with a High Court order prohibiting her from practising as a GP until a fitness-to-practise process by the Irish Medical Council concludes. Dr Regine Grah, who had been operating her own private general practice at Silver Oak Family Practice in Ballywaltrim Heights, Bray, was suspended following an urgent High Court application by the Medical Council last month. In a judgment dated 17 July, the President of the High Court, Mr Justice David Barniville, lifted an in-camera rule that had prevented her being named, saying that the orders were necessary for the protection of the public and patient safety. It followed evidence, yet to be determined, that she was continuing to practise medicine and write prescriptions despite having no professional indemnity insurance.

stories.title: Public pressure forced fuel excise duty shift - Sinn Féin
stories.summary: Sinn Féin's Pearse Doherty has said the Government's move to delay the phasing out of cuts to excise duty on petrol and diesel was the result of public pressure. The cuts were introduced in April following nationwide fuel protests after the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East sent fuel prices soaring. "There is no way that Sinn Féin will stand by and allow that to happen when these fuels prices are increased," he said, noting that - once the temporary cuts have been removed - the price of diesel will increase by 34 cent a litre and petrol by 29 cent. Mr Doherty said Sinn Féin would bring forward an amendment in the Dáil tomorrow calling for no further tax increases on petrol and diesel while fuel prices remain high.

stories.title: Over 2,400 missing after deadly Nepal, China floods
stories.summary: The number of people missing in Nepal and China leapt to more than 2,400, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds. Rescuers were battling through mud even as the threat of new floods loomed, with emergency teams recovering 584 bodies so far - and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India. The new figures came as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. Two Irish citizens, who have been named by the Nepalese Tourism Department as 46-year-old Santosh Sahu and 18-year-old Spandan Sahu, are among those missing.

stories.title: Ban on fisted points and handpass limit to be trialled
stories.summary: Gaelic football's Expert Advisory Group are to trial a series of rule tweaks including a ban on fisted points, a limit on consecutive handpasses and a four-point goal in the upcoming third level Division 1 league. The EAG is chaired by former Roscommon and Mayo manager Kevin McStay and was installed on the recommendation of the Football Review Committee in their final report in 2025, charged with monitoring trends within the game following the sweeping rule changes launched in late 2024. The EAG have proposed nine changes which will be trialled in the Ryan Cup this year. A number of more minor tweaks include increasing the number of substitutes from five to six, proposing a 50-metre advancement if a mark is impeded, the extention of the 40m arc to the end-line, and the alignement of all 50-metre advanced frees to the 13m line rather than the 20m line.

stories.title: Ulster overpower disappointing Connacht at Dexcom
stories.summary: Ulster saved their best performance for last as they picked up their first win of this year's Vodafone Women’s Interprovincial Championship, scoring five tries in a comprehensive 29-10 win against Connacht in the third-place play-off at Dexcom Stadium. Neil Alcorn’s side gained revenge for their 15-10 defeat in round one with a physically dominant performance against their hosts, who looked flat throughout in an error-strewn display. Ireland international Fiona Tuite-O'Sullivan was player of the match from second row, and they took advantage of Connacht’s poor discipline in the first half with four tries and a 24-10 advantage, two of those coming during an expensive yellow card for Connacht flanker Ailish Quinn. Ulster’s defence had been ripped open for 11 tries last week against Leinster, and it looked like they would be in for another long afternoon today when they found themselves back under their own posts within 90 seconds in Galway.

stories.title: Who are pop idols Katseye and why have 2 of them gone on hiatus?
stories.summary: Freelance journalist and broadcaster, writing about music and the arts. One of the most sought-after event tickets this summer has not been for the All-Ireland final, Katie Taylor's Croke Park retirement fight or the long sold-out Electric Picnic, but for the debut Irish performance by Katseye - the latest pop phenomenon to sweep the globe. Irish parents’ WhatsApp groups have descended into panicked meltdowns in search of tickets for the girl group’s gig in Dublin on September 1st, when they will kick off their 'WildWorld’ tour at the 3Arena. Tickets were snapped up within minutes of going on sale back in May: girl groups, as we’ve learned from the popularity of Blackpink, Twice, FLO, Girlset and Say Now, are big business in 2026. It’s akin to Beliebers, Directioners or Lady Gaga’s Little Monsters; Gen Z music fans may recognise elements of the aforementioned Blinks (Blackpink), Swifties (Taylor Swift) or BTS (Army) in the mania surrounding the pop band, whose fans are known as Eyekons. The Los Angeles-based six-piece have become a phenomenon since their formation in 2023, when they were drawn together via an online X Factor-style reality show called Dream Academy (a Netflix documentary about the year-long process was released in 2024). The show, which was launched on YouTube and Weverse, the South Korean fan community platform, was a collaboration between South Korean record label Hybe (the conglomerate behind the unparalleled success of K-Pop boyband BTS) and Geffen Records. The goal? Create a K-Pop-oriented pop group with a Western production style.

stories.title: Not going to EP? These music movies will fit the bill...
stories.summary: Banish the FOMO; there's always next year. In the meantime, you are home and dry - and there's a binge-watch in the offing. Director Walter Hill's CV from 1975 to 1982 - Hard Times, The Driver, The Warriors, The Long Riders, Southern Comfort, and 48 Hrs - is among the most remarkable runs in film history. Crossroads doesn't belong in that hardboiled pantheon, but does it have its charms... Ralph Macchio plays Eugene Martone, the guitar prodigy who heads south in search of a lost blues song. Joe Seneca is Willie Brown, the incorrigible harmonica player with some unfinished business down Mississippi way. "I'm the bluesman, he's from Long Island," deadpans Willie as he counsels and chastises his travelling companion en route to their shared moment of truth in the middle of nowhere. Once again, Macchio hits the chemistry jackpot with an older co-star and the years have been far kinder to Crossroads than the box office was back in 1986. With music by Ry Cooder and a showdown to beat the band, it's an ideal watch for a rainy weekend. Fans of Sinners, take note. The late Ronnie James Dio once said that every band needed to be a democracy led by a dictator. If that's the case, then guitarist Johnny Ramone (John Cummings) was the boss in the Ramones - and made sure everyone remembered it. You're unlikely to forget after seeing this documentary from directors Michael Gramaglia and Jim Fields, a loving but often painful look at one of the most influential bands of the past 50 years. For an outfit whose image and sound have become so associated with togetherness and good times, the Ramones were the complete opposite offstage. Right-wing Johnny ran the band like a business. Liberal singer Joey Ramone (Jeff Hyman) never spoke to Johnny again after his girlfriend married the guitarist. Bassist Dee Dee Ramone (Douglas Colvin) was destroyed by heroin addiction, and after drummer Tommy Ramone (Tom Erdelyi) decided he'd had enough, the Ramones went through a succession of replacements. Perhaps all bands are this dysfunctional, but what makes the Ramones' story so poignant is that they never got the success they truly deserved. Now all the original members are gone. Tommy was the last to die in 2014. Lovers of old-school quality, rejoice - director Nicholas Hytner, writer Alan Bennett, and leading man Ralph Fiennes have just the film for you. This quintessentially British comedy-drama is set in the fictional Yorkshire town of Ramsden in 1916. Conscription has begun, and the glue that keeps the community together, the Ramsden Choral Society, is in danger of losing its hold. Enter Dr Guthrie (Fiennes), a once-celebrated musical director who quotes Goethe and takes no prisoners. The Choral deftly changes gears between humour and poignancy: a laugh-out-loud first half becomes a profound second. The singers and Dr Guthrie lose themselves in the moment while reality waits in the wings. With a soundtrack by five-time Oscar nominee George Fenton (Gandhi, Cry Freedom, Dangerous Liaisons, TV's Planet Earth), the music in this gorgeous-looking film is beautiful - uplifting and elegiac all at once - and deserves to become a familiar friend.

stories.title: 7 ways to minimise dark circles at home
stories.summary: Dark circles are one of the most prolific skin concerns across all ages, and can be down to a myriad of reasons ranging from alcohol to hormones to lack of sleep or simply genetics. "Dark circles are slightly misleading because they are not really one condition," explains aesthetic practitioner Dr David Jack. "What we perceive as darkness underneath the eyes can come from increased melanin in the skin, visible blood vessels through very thin eyelid skin, changes in the underlying anatomy that create shadow or sometimes a mixture of all three." The colour can offer some indication of the cause. Jack says brownish circles are more suggestive of pigmentation, while blue, purple or reddish tones can indicate a greater vascular component.

stories.title: New AI tech considered to tackle wrong-way driving
stories.summary: AI technology and road cameras could be used to alert people more quickly to someone driving the wrong way down a motorway and to help gardaí in their pursuit of the individuals. Minister of State for Road Safety Seán Canney outlined the possible move as he separately said new tougher laws to tackle a spate of recent wrong-way motorway driving incidents will be drafted next week and could be in place by the end of the year. Speaking to reporters at Government Buildings after an initial meeting with gardaí, Transport Infrastructure Ireland and the Road Safety Authority, Minister Canney said it is crucial Ireland makes wrong-way motorway driving an "intolerable" act in this country. The Independent TD said this includes the potential use of AI technology in conjunction with the existing road camera network, which he said could help to better protect the public by providing quicker safety warnings.
